# Calque

> Calque syncs the complete, authorized contents of PostgreSQL 18 tables into the browser, keeps them current through logical replication, and answers the page's queries locally through TypeScript bindings generated from the tables. It is pre-alpha: PostgreSQL 18 is the only source, and Chrome the only browser with benchmark evidence.

This file walks a coding agent through adding Calque to a web application, from an empty database to a page with a live query. Run the steps in order.

## Before you start

- There is no SQL API and no server-side pagination. The page holds every row of each collection its grant allows, and every query runs locally through `client.db.<collection>`.
- Calque is built and measured for working sets of about 100,000 rows. Every page load downloads the whole working set again, so its load time grows with its bytes.
- A collection is one PostgreSQL table with a primary key. `calque inspect` refuses any table or column Calque cannot serve and names the reason; [docs/postgresql.md](docs/postgresql.md) lists the supported types.
- Every column a collection names reaches the browser. If a table holds anything a user must not read, such as a password hash or an internal note, delete that column from the collection's `columns` and its command's `writableColumns` in `calque.config.json`: `calque serve` then publishes the table with a column list that leaves it out, as in `CREATE PUBLICATION calque_app FOR TABLE public.users (id, name)`, so PostgreSQL never sends it. `calque dev` publishes every column of the tables it names.
- A grant gives a page whole tables, or one tenant's rows of them by a tenant column that leads the primary key. Visibility per user or per team needs a projection table the application maintains.
- `int8` columns are `bigint` in TypeScript, so a key is `1n`, not `1`, and `sum()` over any integer column is a `bigint`.
- `query().run()` returns the whole result or rejects with `RESULT_TOO_LARGE`: by default over 1,000 rows or 4 MiB, and at most 10,000 rows and 16 MiB with `run({ maxRows, maxBytes })`. For more, read a window with `window(offset, count)` or subscribe to one.
- A write shows at once and stays optimistic until its change comes back from PostgreSQL.
- The page must be bundled, because the client starts module workers. With Vite, use the `calque()` plugin from `@calque/client/vite`.
- A browser missing an API the client calls gets `UNSUPPORTED_BROWSER`, naming it. The client's browser suites pass in Chromium and Firefox.

## 1. PostgreSQL

The database must be PostgreSQL 18 with `wal_level=logical`, a free replication slot and WAL sender for each Calque server, and UTF-8. Calque connects as a role that is not a superuser, has `REPLICATION` (on Amazon RDS and Aurora, membership in `rds_replication`) and `CREATE` on the database. `calque serve` reads a publication the tables' owner creates, and its role needs only `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on the tables. `calque dev` creates its own publication, so its role owns the tables it serves or is a member of the role that does. For a database on this machine, write `127.0.0.1` in the connection string: any host name, `localhost` included, needs `sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=<absolute path of a CA file>`, as [docs/postgresql.md](docs/postgresql.md#the-database-url) shows. A managed database needs logical replication turned on and its direct endpoint, not a transaction pooler.

Create the role as [docs/postgresql.md](docs/postgresql.md#the-role) shows. For a new table that `calque dev` will serve, as `calque_sync`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE tasks (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, title text NOT NULL, done boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false);
CREATE PUBLICATION calque_app FOR TABLE public.tasks;
```

Set `max_slot_wal_keep_size` on the server, as [docs/postgresql.md](docs/postgresql.md#protecting-the-primarys-disk) shows, so a stopped Calque's replication slot cannot fill the disk.

A collection takes its table's name, which must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$`; rename a table such as `User`, or enroll a projection table. When `calque inspect` refuses something, [docs/postgresql.md](docs/postgresql.md#when-calque-refuses-a-table-or-a-setting) gives the fix for each code. [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md) walks these steps for a person, with an existing database and Vite app.

## 2. The server

`calque` is one Rust binary built from the repository. It needs Rust through rustup, a C compiler, and libpq with `pg_config` on `PATH`. The published image `ghcr.io/calque-sh/calque` runs the same binary: [docs/cli.md](docs/cli.md#running-in-a-container) shows it.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/calque-sh/calque
cargo install --locked --path calque/server/apps/calque
```

## 3. The packages

```sh
npm install @calque/client @calque/react
npm install -D @calque/config
```

`@calque/react` is only for React pages. The Vite plugin needs Vite 8.1.4 or newer, and `@calque/react` React 19 or newer. `@calque/config` renders the typed schema, for the Vite plugin and as `calque-bindings`.

## 4. The typed schema

Every command that connects reads the connection string from `CALQUE_DATABASE_URL`.

```sh
export CALQUE_DATABASE_URL='postgresql://calque_sync:calque_sync@127.0.0.1:5432/app'
calque inspect --source primary --publication calque_app --table public.tasks > calque.inspection.json
calque init --from-inspection calque.inspection.json --application-id my-app
```

The Vite plugin of step 6 renders `calque.config.json` into `calque.generated.ts` and `calque.start.generated.ts` when `vite` starts, whenever the file changes, and before `vite build`, and writes a file only when its render changes; `calque({ bindings: { config, out } })` names other files. Without Vite, `npx calque-bindings` renders them, and its `--config` and `--out` name other files. After the tables change, run both commands again, with `calque init --force`. `calque-bindings --check` writes nothing and exits 1 when either generated file is out of date, for CI. `calque serve` refuses to start when the tables no longer match `calque.config.json`.

## 5. A development server

`calque dev` enrolls a disposable database and serves it on loopback with a development bearer instead of signed grants. It creates its own publication, replication slot and `calque_control` schema in that database, and writes its endpoint and bearer to `.calque-dev/client.env`. Run it from the application's root, because the Vite plugin reads the nearest `.calque-dev` at or above the page's root:

```sh
calque dev --table public.tasks \
  --public-base-url http://127.0.0.1:5173/_calque/ \
  --acknowledge-disposable-source
```

It allows the origin `http://127.0.0.1:5173` unless `--allow-origin` names another, and `--public-base-url` is the Vite proxy's address, which every URL it hands the page names. `calque destroy --state-dir .calque-dev --yes` removes what it created.

## 6. The page

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { calque } from "@calque/client/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [calque()],
  server: { host: "127.0.0.1", port: 5173, strictPort: true },
});
```

Under `vite`, the plugin renders the connection into the page and proxies `/_calque/` to `calque dev`, so the page never holds the development bearer:

```ts
// main.ts
import { createSyncClient, eq } from "@calque/client";
import { renderedConnection } from "@calque/client/bootstrap-start";
import { schema } from "./calque.generated.js";

const { endpoint, bearerToken } = renderedConnection();
const client = createSyncClient({
  endpoint,
  auth: () => ({ bearerToken }),
  schema,
});

const open = await client.db.tasks.query().where(eq("done", false)).run();

const live = client.db.tasks.query().orderBy("id").subscribe();
live.subscribe(() => {
  const snapshot = live.getSnapshot();
  if (snapshot.status === "ready") render(snapshot.result);
});

await client.db.tasks.update({ id: 1n }, { done: true });
```

In React, put the client in `SyncProvider` and read with `useLiveQuery`; see [client/packages/react/README.md](client/packages/react/README.md).

## 7. Production

`calque serve` replaces `calque dev`. It verifies short-lived grants that the application's backend signs with an Ed25519 key, and mints none. The page's `auth()` returns the grant as `bearerToken`, and the client is created with `grantVerificationKey`, the public half of that signing key, so a revocation empties the page at once. [docs/self-host.md](docs/self-host.md) runs it behind HTTPS from a clean checkout; [spec/dataset-grant-v1.md](spec/dataset-grant-v1.md) defines the grant, and `npm install @calque/grant` gives a Node backend `calque-grant keygen` to create the signing key and `mintGrant` to sign a grant ([client/packages/grant](client/packages/grant)).
